frontend/src/store/playerBus.ts.summary: Removed the retired scope toggle: deleted the AltScope type, the altScope field from PlayerBusState/LoadAndPlayOptions/IDLE_STATE, and the switchScope() function entirely. scope remains as an informational field only; it no longer drives any bus behavior.

frontend/src/app/layout/PlayerBar.tsx.summary: Replaced the scope-driven showWave predicate (forceWave ?? scope === 'segment') with a duration-driven one (forceWave ?? fitsLegibly(duration, measuredWidth)) backed by a new ResizeObserver measuring the scrub container. Removed the scope-toggle JSX block (player-scope-toggle/pill/badge) and the switchScope/altScope imports and destructure.

frontend/src/app/layout/playerRepresenta.summary: New pure-function module implementing the audio-player.md 1.6.0 duration-driven scrub representation decision: fitsLegibly(durationSec, barWidthPx), plus PX_PER_SEC_FLOOR (3) and DURATION_BOOTSTRAP (120) constants. Scope-blind by construction (no scope parameter).

frontend/src/pages/Book/stages/ReviewSta.summary: playChapter(audioUrl, title) dropped its third segmentAltScope parameter and no longer imports AltScope or passes altScope into loadAndPlay — the Review adapter no longer registers a scope-toggle alternate source.
Removed the segmentAltScope construction (first-rendered-segment lookup) that fed the old scope toggle; handleChapterSelect now calls playChapter(audioUrl, chapter.title) only.

frontend/src/theme/components.css.summary: Deleted .player-scope-badge, .player-scope-toggle, .player-scope-pill, .player-scope-pill--active and related selectors; refreshed nearby comments that described wave-vs-bar as scope-driven.

flow_impact: Global PlayerBar scrub representation (waveform vs. plain seek bar) is now decided purely by clip duration + measured bar width (fitsLegibly), never by playerBus.scope; the segment/chapter scope toggle UI and bus fields are fully retired, closing the audio-player.md 1.6.0 spec-ahead-of-code gap for Workload 1. No change to playback/transport/single-audio-owner behavior.
